java.say: The program needs the database. It cannot make one itself, because the constructor is private. So it asks the class.
getInstance() is static, so it runs on the class, without an object. The first time, there is no object yet.
So it makes the one object and keeps it in the static field.
It returns that object. Every later call skips the if and returns the same object.
db now points to the one Database. Every caller that asks gets this same object.
